description: One conversation for everybody the board is shared with. Deploy it, add the people to its member list, and each of them writes as themselves: who said a thing is the caller the server verified, never a field of the request, so nobody can post in somebody else's name. The thread lives in the board's own database on the server, and the facade broadcasts it, so a message one person sends reaches everybody attached at once — no timer, no reload. Clearing the history is the owner's. Needs an hkp-node kept under the name `node`.

state.schema:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS message (
  id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  -- What the board's member list called them when they wrote it, so a later
  -- rename does not rewrite what was already said.
  author TEXT,
  -- The address of whoever wrote it, as the server that signed them in said.
  email  TEXT,
  text   TEXT NOT NULL,
  at     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
-- A message says who wrote it. One arriving from nobody is refused with the
-- reason, rather than kept as an anonymous line nobody can answer.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS a_message_has_an_author
BEFORE INSERT ON message
WHEN NEW.email IS NULL
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'sign in to write — a message is signed with who you are');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS a_message_fits_on_a_screen
BEFORE INSERT ON message
WHEN length(NEW.text) > 2000
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'that is longer than 2000 characters — split it into a few messages');
END;
state.statement:
INSERT INTO message (author, email, text)
-- Members are called what the owner's list calls them. An owner the list
-- does not name is the owner; their address is never shown to anybody.
SELECT coalesce($caller_name, CASE WHEN $caller_role = 'owner' THEN 'Owner' END),
       $caller_email,
       trim($text)
 WHERE $intent = 'post'
   AND trim(coalesce($text, '')) <> ''

-- The owner's alone: a member asking is a member asking, and deletes nothing.
DELETE FROM message
 WHERE $intent = 'clear'
   AND $caller_role = 'owner'

-- The latest 200, oldest first, as a thread reads. The address stays in
-- the table: what is sent to everybody is the name.
SELECT id, author, text,
       CASE WHEN date(at) = date('now')
            THEN strftime('%H:%M', at)
            ELSE strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M', at)
       END AS time
  FROM (SELECT * FROM message ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 200)
 ORDER BY id
